title: TurfBot
subtitle: A LangGraph assistant on Claude that reads the whole ERP within each user's roles
summary: TurfBot is a Python 3.12 Flask application with a LangGraph agent on Claude (Anthropic Messages API). It answers questions from live ERP data through 56 read-only tools, offering each user only the tools of the modules their Keycloak roles open, and records every question, lookup and API call in an append-only audit trail with token costs.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Users sign in with the same turfclub-web client through PKCE; the code verifier and nonce travel inside a signed, time-limited state parameter, so the Flask app keeps no login state between the redirect and the callback.

The services trust svc-chatbot with SVC_READ, so the chatbot is the policy enforcement point: Claude is given only the tools of modules the user may open, and the tools node checks again before running anything. A tool the model was not given is refused and logged as DENIED.

Prompt caching keeps it affordable: tool definitions (sorted, breakpoint on the last) and the stable system instructions are cached; the per-request block with today's date and the user's modules comes after the breakpoint.

terms.definition: LangGraph StateGraph: agent → tools → agent until Claude answers, capped at MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS.
A read-only call to one module's /api/v1 with a JSON-schema input, tagged with its module.
<MODULE>_VIEW / _MANAGE opens a module's tools; TC_AUDITOR / TC_ADMIN open the audit tools.
Repeated prefix (tools + instructions) read from cache at a fraction of the input price.
Schema chatbot: conversation, message, tool_call, llm_usage, guarded append-only.

sections.intro: Solid arrows are live REST calls, dotted arrows are accounting events or the AR import, plain lines are shared master data. Click a box to open that module.

sections.title: Design decisions
items: Read-only by design: change requests are answered with where in the ERP to make the change.
Results are cut for the model (100 rows / 12,000 characters) but stored in full for the Excel export.
History is replayed as plain text; the model looks figures up again for fresh data.

sections.title: Tools Claude can use
sections.intro: Each tool is offered only to users whose roles open its module. Audit tools need TC_AUDITOR or TC_ADMIN.
rows: List the club's legal entities (id, code, name, base currency).
List the club's venues (racecourses and sites) with their legal entity and time zone.
Search the shared party register (people and organisations: owners, trainers, jockeys, suppliers, members, customers) by name, external reference or email. Returns ids, contact details and addresses.
Full details of one party by id, including all addresses.
Open / closed days of a venue for one month (with notes).
The allowed values of a reference-data domain, e.g. COUNTRY, CURRENCY, TAX_CODE, HORSE_BREED, UOM, ITEM_CATEGORY_CLASS, RACE_OFFICIAL_ROLE.

Audit trail of a party: who changed its details or any of its addresses, when, and the before / after value of every changed field. Use for questions like 'who changed X's address last week'. Accepts a party name or id; when several parties match the name, the candidates are returned so you can ask which one.

Search the ERP-wide audit trail (every insert / update / delete on audited tables), newest first. Filter by database schema (e.g. enterprise_core, financial_ap, horse_registry), table, record id, actor (Keycloak username) and date range.
Chart of accounts of a legal entity (code, name, type, posting flag). Optional text filter.
Trial balance (debits, credits and balance per account) for a date range from posted journals.
One GL journal with its lines, by journal id.
Search registered horses by name or registration number.
Full horse record by id: pedigree, colour, breed, documents, medical summary, current owners.
Owners of a horse and their percentage shares on a date (default today).
Whether a horse may race on a date, and the reasons if not.
Racing licences (jockey, trainer, owner, official) with holder, number, validity and status.
Is a party's licence of a type valid on a date (default today)?
The trainer assigned to a horse on a date (default today).
Racing profile of a party: licences, jockey contracts, horses in training.
Race meetings between two dates (inclusive) with venue and status.

The race card: every race of a meeting with start time, distance, surface, purse, runners (saddlecloth, draw, horse, jockey, trainer, weight) and officials. Give the meeting date (resolve words like 'Saturday' to a date first) or a meeting id; with neither, the next meeting from today is used.
One race by id: details, runners, officials and results if run.
Finishing order of a race, finish times, disqualifications and whether the result is official.
Tote pools of a race: bet type, takeout, total staked, status and declared dividends.
Winning tickets of a race with dividend and paid status.
One wagering ticket by id: selections, stake, channel, status.
Prize money split by finishing position for a race.
Prize awards of a race: horse, payee (owner / trainer / jockey), amount, status.
All prize awards paid or payable to a party (owner, trainer or jockey).
Payout of a winning ticket: gross, tax withheld, net, status.
Membership plans with annual fee and guest allowance.
Search club members by name, member number or email.
One member with dependents and renewal history.
Whether a member (by member id, or a member's or dependent's party id) is in good standing, with the reasons if not.
Restaurants, bars and function rooms with capacity.
Menu of an outlet with prices and tax codes.
Table reservations on a day (default today).
Upcoming club events with capacity, places booked, places left and price.
Stock items (SKU, description, category, unit, standard cost, reorder point). Optional text filter.
Stores and stock locations by venue.
Quantity and value on hand by item and location. Filter by item text and / or location code.
Items at or below their reorder point (stock across all locations) with the suggested order quantity.
Suppliers with code, payment terms, tax id and status. Optional text filter.
Purchase orders (newest first) with supplier, total, status and lines.
One purchase order with its lines, by id.
One goods receipt with accepted / rejected quantities, by id.
Supplier invoices (newest first, up to 200) with balance and status. Filter by status and supplier text.

What the club owes suppliers: open (approved, posted or part-paid) supplier invoices with a balance, totals by currency and days overdue, optionally for one supplier. Draft invoices not yet approved are listed separately.
One supplier invoice with lines and payments, by id.
Accounts payable ageing buckets on a date, reconciled to GL account 2100.
Customer invoices (stabling, fees, member charges...) with balance and status. Filter by status, customer text and source module (e.g. MEMBERSHIP, HOSPITALITY, RACING).
What a customer owes the club: open invoices and total, by customer name or party id.
One customer invoice with lines and receipts, by id.
Accounts receivable ageing buckets on a date, reconciled to GL accounts 1200 / 1210.
Book balance of every bank account, last statement date and closing balance, unmatched lines.
Imported bank statement lines of a bank account (use cash_position for account ids).

episode.title: Building a role-aware ERP assistant with LangGraph and Claude

Enforce user permissions with a service account
Use prompt caching and record cost per answer

Tool registry and the role filter
LangGraph agent and tools nodes, the second permission check
Usage and audit dashboard, Excel export of tool rows
